body: Was wondering if you had any updates to this status?
It was resolved by [this commit](https://github.com/celery/celery/commit/ec1fd31e9baed79d54c3e36b5f5d37e6e70a246f). Are you seeing it in version 4.0.2 ?

Yes I'm using 4.0.2 and was running into a few issues. I'm using the redid broker as well but the task didn't restart once I killed it. I'd have to manually kick start the celery workers and the tasks are lost in the process.
I am seeing this on version 4.1.0

I'm can't get this to work as well (using both `acks_late = True` and `reject_on_worker_lost = True`). Is there some special configuration needed for this to work?
I see that @georgepsarakis commented this was supposed to be fixed in commit:
https://github.com/celery/celery/issues/3541#issuecomment-312446892

Can someone explain how this flag is supposed to work in theory, given the code base?
I see the flag is only checked  in [request.py](https://github.com/celery/celery/blob/master/celery/worker/request.py#L372) but this looks like it is only called when it's being consumed. How is the task supposed to be rescheduled if a process "[abruptly exits](http://docs.celeryproject.org/en/latest/userguide/configuration.html#task-reject-on-worker-lost)" i.e. worker node goes down completely?

@wongwill86 I tried to use `acks_late = True` and `reject_on_worker_lost = True` with a Redis broker and it didn't work. But with RabbitMQ as a broker it works properly.

Also I found [this example](https://gist.github.com/mlavin/6671079) with a fixed Redis transport (but didn't try to use) and [one comment on Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/6577218/how-to-guarantee-message-delivery-with-celery#comment8288511_6577218) about Redis (maybe it is relevant at present).

If you are going to use Celery chords and want to use options `acks_late` and `reject_on_worker_lost` with them, apply this options to all tasks in a chord and [use Memcached or Redis as  a `result_backend`](http://docs.celeryproject.org/en/master/userguide/canvas.html#chord-important-notes)

> Tasks used within a chord must not ignore their results. If the result backend is disabled for any task (header or body) in your chord you should read “Important Notes.” Chords are not currently supported with the RPC result backend.

And [there is an another way](https://stackoverflow.com/a/5339543/5157209) to recover tasks after a crash.

Thanks for the tip @Sinkler!

I was indeed using a Redis broker. For now it seems to be working with RabbitMQ so I'll use that for now.

Hi, I am seeing this issue on celery `5.0.2` with a redis `5.0.9` backend (with `--appendonly yes`). Like the OP, I confirm `reject_on_worker_lost == True` by printing it in the task, kill the worker during the task, but the other worker does not pick up the task. 

Would it be possible to reopen this issue?

Hi again, I've used to code in the OP to reproduce a simple setup using celery 5.0.5 and redis 6.2.0 without any `ResultsBackend` by sending SIGKILL signals to the celery worker  and I could not reproduce the issue: celery correctly rejects the task upon losing the worker, I will investigate further.
thanks let us know the update.

I have not managed to reproduce the issue, I think we can close this.

(I did find [a couple of mistakes in the documentation](https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/6658) while searching though so this was not in vain)
I have the same issue. I've created this repository so it's easier to reproduce this bug: https://github.com/jozo/celery-task_reject_on_worker_lost

```yaml
  environment:
    REMAP_SIGTERM: 'SIGQUIT'
```

In the `celery` service of your example help?
